title: Design review: offline mode
description: App Store screenshot meeting: Kestrel Labs prepares the version two beta. Turns are scheduled back to back from measured Kokoro durations. The first 14 s are silent so the recording, started once the call is live, catches every line.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: Thanks for joining. I have three screens for offline mode: the banner, the schedule, and what happens when you try to edit.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: It sits at the top of the schedule. It says you're offline, and the schedule was last updated at a given time. It's amber, not red, because nothing is broken.

turns.speaker: tomas
turns.text: Good. Can it show when we're syncing again, so people know their view is fresh?

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: Yes. When you reconnect it turns blue for a moment and says up to date.

turns.speaker: amara
turns.text: And the edit case? In the beta, editing offline is off.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: Right. If you tap an appointment offline, the edit button is greyed out, with one line underneath: you can edit this when you're back online.

turns.speaker: tomas
turns.text: One worry. Receptionists at the clinic work on old tablets. Is the contrast on the amber banner strong enough?

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: I checked it against the accessibility guidelines, and it passes. I also tested it at the largest text size.

turns.speaker: amara
turns.text: Then I'm happy. Let's approve the banner and the disabled edit state for the beta.

turns.speaker: hannah
turns.text: Great. I'll hand the final files to Tomás tomorrow.

turns.speaker: tomas
turns.text: And I'll add the banner to this week's build so Priya can start testing it.
